# apple_app_store_version (Resource)

Manages one release of an app on one platform.

A version owns everything that describes a particular release rather than the app itself: the version string, the copyright line, how it is released once approved, and — through `apple_app_store_version_localization` — the description, keywords and release notes. What describes the app across releases (name, subtitle, categories, age rating) belongs to `apple_app_info` and `apple_app_info_localization`.

An app can hold only **one editable version per platform** at a time; Apple answers a second with a 409 naming the one already being prepared. Import the existing one rather than creating another.

Only an editable version can be deleted. A version that has been released, or is in review, is part of the app's history — destroying it warns and drops it from state.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "apple_apps" "example" {
  bundle_id = "com.example.app"
}

# An app can hold only one editable version per platform at a time; Apple
# answers a second with a 409 naming the one already being prepared. Import the
# existing one rather than creating another.
resource "apple_app_store_version" "v1" {
  app_id         = data.apple_apps.example.apps[0].id
  platform       = "IOS"
  version_string = "1.0"

  copyright = "2026 AO Studio"

  # AFTER_APPROVAL is "release automatically"; MANUAL holds the approved version
  # until it is released by hand.
  release_type = "MANUAL"
}

# A scheduled release needs a full ISO 8601 timestamp with seconds and a zone,
# not a plain date.
resource "apple_app_store_version" "v2" {
  app_id         = data.apple_apps.example.apps[0].id
  platform       = "IOS"
  version_string = "2.0"

  copyright             = "2026 AO Studio"
  release_type          = "SCHEDULED"
  earliest_release_date = "2026-03-01T08:00:00-07:00"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `app_id` (String) The Apple ID of the app this version belongs to. Read it from the `apple_apps` data source. Cannot be changed.
- `platform` (String) The platform this version is for: `IOS`, `MAC_OS`, `TV_OS` or `VISION_OS`. Note that this is a different list from an `apple_bundle_id`'s platform — Apple accepts `TV_OS` and `VISION_OS` here and rejects both there. Absent from Apple's update request, so changing it replaces the version.
- `version_string` (String) The version number customers see, such as `1.0` or `2.14.3`. Up to three dot-separated numbers. Updatable in place while the version is editable, and it must match the `CFBundleShortVersionString` of the build attached to it.

### Optional

- `copyright` (String) The copyright line shown on the product page, conventionally the year and the rights holder — `2026 AO Studio`. Apple wants the year alone, not a `©` symbol, which it adds itself.
- `earliest_release_date` (String) When a `SCHEDULED` release goes live, as an ISO 8601 timestamp with seconds and a zone — `2026-03-01T08:00:00-07:00`. Ignored unless `release_type` is `SCHEDULED`.
- `release_type` (String) How the version is released once App Review approves it:

- `AFTER_APPROVAL` — released automatically the moment it passes review.
- `MANUAL` — held until released by hand in App Store Connect.
- `SCHEDULED` — released at `earliest_release_date`.

This is the attribute an "automatic release" setting maps onto: automatic is `AFTER_APPROVAL`, manual is `MANUAL`.
- `review_type` (String) Which review queue the version goes through: `APP_STORE` or `NOTARIZATION`. Notarization is for Mac software distributed outside the App Store.
- `uses_idfa` (Boolean) Whether the app uses the Advertising Identifier. Apple derives this from the binary for recent submissions and rejects a value that contradicts it.

### Read-Only

- `app_version_state` (String) Where the version stands, for example `PREPARE_FOR_SUBMISSION`, `WAITING_FOR_REVIEW` or `READY_FOR_DISTRIBUTION`. Apple's, never the provider's.
- `created_date` (String) When Apple created the version record.
- `downloadable` (Boolean) Whether the version is currently downloadable from the App Store.
- `id` (String) The unique Apple-generated identifier for the version.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# A bare Apple version ID.
terraform import apple_app_store_version.v1 8a41f2c7-93b6-4e5d-a1c8-2f7e6b4d0931

# Or the composite form -- all three parts, because the same version string
# exists once per platform.
terraform import apple_app_store_version.v1 6478291043/IOS/1.0
```
